Observations: Channel 0 (agent) has large W1 norms only on row 8, the bottom row of the playable area: row 8, col 1 = 8.24, col 2 = 5.33, col 7 = 5.95, col 8 = 9.73, while all other rows are near 0.3â0.4. This strongly suggests the agent is a bottom-row paddle/player that moves horizontally. Channel 1 (moving objects) is large throughout rows 1â7, especially row 4: col 3 = 17.41, col 7 = 16.12, row 3 col 5 = 15.29, row 4 col 1 = 15.48. That fits a ball moving around the playfield. Channel 2 (reward targets) is large only in rows 1â3: row 3 col 1 = 6.06, row 3 col 7 = 6.20, row 1 col 6 = 2.97, etc. That is a static block of targets at the top. Channel 3 (obstacles) is high only on the border: max 0.75 on row/column 0 and 9, inner cells mostly ~0.3â0.4. So there are no inner obstacles, only walls. Channel 4 (previous frame) is large in the middle/lower playfield, e.g. row 7 col 4 = 19.87, row 7 col 5 = 18.67, row 6 col 4 = 14.35, row 6 col 5 = 14.51, consistent with tracking the previous ball/paddle positions. The output layer W3/b3 is omitted, so I cannot quote action biases, but the action set plus the bottom-row agent strongly implies left/right/no-op are the meaningful controls.

Reasoning: A bottom-row movable agent, a moving ball-like object, and static reward targets in the top rows is the classic structure of Breakout. Pong is ruled out because there are no top-row reward targets. Space Invaders is less likely because there are no inner obstacles/shields and the reward targets are static top-row blocks rather than moving enemies. Maze/collectible games are ruled out by the agent being confined to row 8 and by the lack of inner obstacle structure. The channel maps therefore point to an Atari-style brick-breaker: the paddle at the bottom bounces a ball to destroy bricks at the top.

Game: Breakout / Atari-style brick-breaker.

Description: The agent controls a paddle on the bottom row, moving left or right to bounce a ball. Reward comes from hitting and clearing bricks in the top rows; missing the ball likely ends the episode.

Confidence: 94%
